## TL;DR

Implemented a guarded way to preserve a good review verdict after the task branch merges main, but only when every net changed path in the merge commit exactly matches the merge-time main parent. Added a read-only classifier route for the UI, a guarded server mutation, the `repoos review keep <id>` CLI path, and action buttons on the close-out failure card and Debug conflict view. Keeping the verdict refreshes the handoff snapshot and review lock, records the old and new SHA in task activity, then submits the ordinary close-out request.

## Work and rationale

The starting worktree already contained the first classifier, CLI wiring, mutation endpoint, and basic tests, but it had no UI integration or read-only endpoint for deciding when to display the action. I completed the UI path by having the failure card periodically check whether the reviewed SHA and current task tip meet the safe-merge rule. In the Debug conflict view, the existing re-check action also refreshes that classification. Both controls only appear when the server says the merge is safe; the mutation endpoint repeats the proof, so a stale UI result cannot authorize an unsafe keep.

The classifier requires a clean worktree, a two-parent merge commit with the reviewed SHA on its task-side ancestry, and at least one net changed path. Every path changed between the reviewed SHA and merge tip must resolve to the same object as that path at the merge's main-side parent. This conservatively covers main's own additions and changes while refusing task-side content layered into the merge. I changed ancestry verification to use `GitWorker.isAncestor`, keeping it within the existing git abstraction.

Before refreshing the lock, the mutation checks that the task is still in review, the lock is still in review state, no review is running, and the shared root/close-out locks are available. The history note records the precise old and new SHA. The client then invokes the normal close-out endpoint, so all existing landability and integration gates still apply.

## Approaches tried

I first used the existing failure card and Debug conflict view rather than adding a new panel or confirmation dialog. The UI only displays an action after a fresh server classification, while the CLI and POST endpoint remain authoritative. No native confirmation dialog is needed because the button label directly states the action and the endpoint refuses anything outside the proof.

I ran the required changed-path check. The first run found formatter issues, so I applied the repository formatter and reran the check. One subsequent remote run reported a failure in the existing direct-serve guard test; the same test had passed in the first remote run and passed in an isolated local run. A further complete rerun passed.

## Challenges and blockers

The changed-path check uses a remote runner and ran for several minutes. The direct-serve guard failure provided only a test name, with no failed assertion details. Searching the exact test text found no public results. Local runtime inspection showed Node v26.13.1, Bun 1.4.4, and the actual Node executable at `/Users/nick/.vite-plus/bin/node`; the isolated test passed. The final full run also passed remotely. No unresolved implementation blocker remains.

## Key learnings

A review lock should only move when the merge commit itself proves what was incorporated. Comparing net paths to the merge-time main parent gives a straightforward conservative test and avoids trying to infer intent from commit messages or conflict metadata. The proof belongs on both the display and mutation paths: the UI can guide the user, while the server must revalidate because branch state can change between a poll and a click.

The existing handoff refresh helper keeps the snapshot and review lock synchronized, and task activity provides the durable human-readable audit trail. A narrowly scoped retry of the existing close-out flow preserves all current close-out checks after the verdict is kept.
